walkthroughs.body_html:
Issues and Debates — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Issues and Debates brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Issues and Debates.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many principles does the BPS Code of Ethics contain?
If deception is used, what must be provided afterwards?
options: Debrief
Reward
Public apology
Withdrawal fee

mcqs.q: Why does the cognitive approach use INFERENCE?
options: Because cognitive psychologists guess instead of measuring.
Because brain scans are unreliable.
The id (pleasure principle).
Mental processes cannot be directly observed, so they are inferred from behaviour.

mcqs.q: Which part of the psyche operates on the reality principle?
options: The id (pleasure principle).
The superego (moral principle).
The ego.
Because brain scans are unreliable.
Being directly rewarded for copying someone.
Reinforcing yourself mentally.
Learning by observing the consequences others receive for behaviour.
The id (pleasure principle).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Debrief”?
options: Withholding information or misleading participants; permitted only if no alternative and harm is minimal.
Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.
Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Participants must be free to leave at any point without penalty, including withdrawing their data.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “BPS code (2021)”?
options: Withholding information or misleading participants; permitted only if no alternative and harm is minimal.
Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.
British Psychological Society Code of Ethics and Conduct sets four principles: respect, competence, responsibility, integrity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Right to withdraw”?
options: British Psychological Society Code of Ethics and Conduct sets four principles: respect, competence, responsibility, integrity.
Participants must be free to leave at any point without penalty, including withdrawing their data.
Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Protection from harm”?
options: Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.
Participants must be protected from physical and psychological harm beyond everyday experience.
Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Participants must be free to leave at any point without penalty, including withdrawing their data.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Informed consent”?
options: Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Participants must be protected from physical and psychological harm beyond everyday experience.
Participants must be free to leave at any point without penalty, including withdrawing their data.
British Psychological Society Code of Ethics and Conduct sets four principles: respect, competence, responsibility, integrity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Deception”?
options: British Psychological Society Code of Ethics and Conduct sets four principles: respect, competence, responsibility, integrity.
Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Withholding information or misleading participants; permitted only if no alternative and harm is minimal.
Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.

mcqs.q: How many ethical principles are in the current BPS Code?
options: 3 principles
2 principles
5 principles
4 principles
